question: What does it mean for a probe to settle as N grows, and for all four probes to agree by the Einstein relation d_s = 2 d_f / d_w, such that every exact lattice of the calibration table settles on every probe it is held to and reaches the fifth band where it is held on all four, a random graph scores nothing and a small world does not settle? (the operator, 2026-11-11 05:07: every probe that settles to a value as N grows adds to the score, the tree line left out, a kept lattice adds too, more probes more points; 2026-11-14 19:39: a 5th band where all probes agree by the Einstein law)
a_reading: a probe reads a size when more than half of its three seeds read a value there (the fleet's rule, observability/space_score._probe); its reading is the mean of the seeds that read
the_sizes: from the smallest size at or above 4,096, the next size is the smallest at least three times the last: the fleet's ladder steps by four, and a table family or a judged structure built at other sizes is read at the sizes nearest that step. A pair is two such sizes one after the other.
settles: a probe settles at a pair when it reads at both sizes and |x_b - x_a| <= r(p, b) * (x_a + x_b) / 2, r the probe's relative margin at the pair's larger size
einstein: all four probes agree at a pair when all four settle there and, at the larger size, both |d_s - 2 d_V / d_w| and |d_s - 2 d_B / d_w| are at most tau * d_s: d_V and d_B are each the mass dimension d_f of the relation
points: at a pair, the probes that settle (0 to 4) and one more where all four agree: 0 to 5; the fifth is the landscape's 5th band

training.families: every family of table_holds' with_a_dimension, the lattices of one to four dimensions, both quotients, the Sierpinski gasket and carpet and the uniform random tree, each probe at the sizes table_holds holds it at (from its from_nodes)
training.triples: seeds 0, 1, 2; 3, 4, 5; 6, 7, 8 of a size the table holds ten seeds at, and 0, 1, 2 alone where it holds three: a fleet rung's three seeds
training.margin_rule: r(p, b) is the smallest value of the grid that is at least twice the widest training step at that level (the table's exact lattices and fractals, criterion 1's training set and triples unchanged): the factor of two the stability score has used for a step against its noise floor (research/stability_score.TOLERANCE_MULTIPLIER), so a seed's sampling noise has room that the exact lattices' near-identical seeds did not show
training.tau_rule: tau is the smallest value of its grid that is at least every training triple's larger relative Einstein residual, max(|d_s - 2 d_V / d_w|, |d_s - 2 d_B / d_w|) / d_s, at a size the table holds all four probes at for its family. A residual above the grid's largest value sets tau to it and is listed.
